docs.title: RWCheck
docs.text:
Fast Retraction Watch lookup — REST API, CLI, and Python library.

RWCheck lets you check DOIs and PubMed IDs against the Retraction Watch dataset in milliseconds. It ships as:

  • A command-line tool (rwcheck) for interactive use and scripting
  • A Python library (import rwcheck) for programmatic access
  • A self-hosted REST API (FastAPI) with a built-in browser UI

All lookups are served from a local SQLite database built from the Retraction Watch CSV dataset, so there are no external API calls at query time.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
pip install rwcheck

# Download & build the local database (one-time setup)
rwcheck update

# Check a DOI
rwcheck doi 10.1038/nature12345

# Check a PubMed ID
rwcheck pmid 12345678

docs.title: Features
docs.text: Feature Details DOI lookup Normalises URL/bare DOIs; case-insensitive PMID lookup Integer or string input Batch DOI/PMID Text file (one per line) or CSV with --col BibTeX check Extracts DOIs & PMIDs from every entry, writes MD + HTML + JSON reports Python API check_doi(), check_pmid(), check_batch() REST API FastAPI with OpenAPI docs, rate limiting, background auto-update Self-hosted Single Docker container; data volume for the SQLite DB Offline No network calls at query time after initial DB build

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
retraction_watch.csv (GitLab)
         │
         ▼  rwcheck update / build-rw-db
    data/rw.sqlite
         │
    ┌────┴────────────────────┐
    │   rwcheck CLI           │  ← you run commands here
    │   rwcheck Python API    │  ← import rwcheck
    │   REST API (FastAPI)    │  ← curl / browser
    └─────────────────────────┘
  1. Build — rwcheck update downloads the CSV and ingests it into a local SQLite file.
  2. Query — Every lookup is a fast indexed SQL query against the local DB.
  3. Update — Run rwcheck update periodically (or let the API's background scheduler handle it).

docs.title: License
docs.text: MIT. The underlying Retraction Watch dataset is provided by the Center for Scientific Integrity under their terms.

docs.title: CLI Reference
docs.text:
The rwcheck command-line tool checks DOIs and PubMed IDs against the local Retraction Watch database.

Usage: rwcheck [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

  Check DOIs/PMIDs against the Retraction Watch dataset.

Options:
  --version   Show version and exit.
  --help      Show this message and exit.

Commands:
  doi         Check a single DOI.
  pmid        Check a single PubMed ID.
  batch-doi   Batch-check DOIs from a text or CSV file.
  batch-pmid  Batch-check PMIDs from a text or CSV file.
  batch-bib   Check all references in a BibTeX file.
  update      Download the latest dataset and rebuild the local DB.

docs.title: Global options
docs.text:
Option Description --version Print rwcheck <version> and exit --help Show help and exit

All commands share two common options for choosing the data source:

Option Default Description --db PATH data/rw.sqlite Path to the local SQLite database --api URL (none) Delegate lookups to a remote rwcheck REST API instead of the local DB

docs.title: rwcheck doi
docs.text:
Check whether a single DOI appears in Retraction Watch.

rwcheck doi DOI [--db PATH] [--api URL] [--json]

Arguments

Argument Description DOI DOI to check. URL prefixes (https://doi.org/) and doi: prefixes are stripped automatically.

Options

Option Description --json Output raw JSON instead of the formatted table

Examples

# Basic check
rwcheck doi 10.1038/nature12345

# Output JSON
rwcheck doi 10.1038/nature12345 --json

# Use a different DB path
rwcheck doi 10.1038/nature12345 --db /opt/rw/data/rw.sqlite

# Delegate to a remote API
rwcheck doi 10.1038/nature12345 --api http://localhost:8000

Output (table mode)

NOT FOUND  query=10.1038/nature12345  (no retraction records)
Dataset: abc123... | rows=45231 | built=2024-06-01T12:00:00

If the DOI is retracted:

RETRACTED  query=10.1016/j.cell.2009.10.015  (1 record(s))
  Record ID         12345
  Title             Example Paper Title
  Journal           Cell
  Nature            Retraction
  Reason            Data Fabrication
  Retraction Date   2010-01-15
  Original DOI      10.1016/j.cell.2009.10.015
  Retraction DOI    10.1016/j.cell.2010.01.010

docs.title: rwcheck pmid
docs.text:
Check whether a single PubMed ID appears in Retraction Watch.

rwcheck pmid PMID [--db PATH] [--api URL] [--json]

Arguments

Argument Description PMID PubMed ID (integer or numeric string).

Options

Same as rwcheck doi.

Examples

rwcheck pmid 12345678
rwcheck pmid 12345678 --json
rwcheck pmid 12345678 --api http://localhost:8000

docs.title: rwcheck batch-doi
docs.text:
Batch-check DOIs from a plain-text file (one per line) or a CSV/TSV file.

rwcheck batch-doi FILE [--db PATH] [--api URL] [--out FORMAT] [--col COLUMN] [--report-dir DIR]

Arguments

Argument Description FILE Path to a .txt, .csv, or .tsv file containing DOIs.

Options

Option Default Description --out FORMAT table Output format: table, json, or tsv --col COLUMN first column CSV column name that contains DOIs --report-dir DIR same dir as input Directory to write report files

Input formats

Plain text (one DOI per line, # comments ignored):

# My references
10.1038/nature12345
10.1016/j.cell.2009.10.015
https://doi.org/10.1007/s00248-019-01449-w

CSV with a doi column:

doi,title
10.1038/nature12345,Paper 1
10.1016/j.cell.2009.10.015,Paper 2

rwcheck batch-doi papers.csv --col doi

Output formats

TableJSONTSV 

rwcheck batch-doi dois.txt
Coloured summary printed to stdout + three report files written.

rwcheck batch-doi dois.txt --out json
Full JSON to stdout (no report files printed to stdout).

rwcheck batch-doi dois.txt --out tsv > results.tsv
One row per match; header row included.

Report files

Three files are always written (regardless of --out):

File Description <stem>_rwcheck.md Human-readable Markdown report <stem>_rwcheck.html Self-contained HTML report <stem>_rwcheck.json Machine-readable JSON with full match details

docs.title: rwcheck batch-pmid
docs.text:
Batch-check PMIDs from a plain-text file or CSV/TSV. Same interface as batch-doi.

rwcheck batch-pmid FILE [--db PATH] [--api URL] [--out FORMAT] [--col COLUMN] [--report-dir DIR]

Non-integer lines are silently skipped. A count of skipped entries is shown in table mode.

Examples

# Plain text file
rwcheck batch-pmid pmids.txt

# CSV with explicit column
rwcheck batch-pmid refs.csv --col pubmed_id --out tsv > results.tsv

# Write reports to a specific directory
rwcheck batch-pmid pmids.txt --report-dir ./reports/

docs.title: rwcheck batch-bib
docs.text:
Parse a BibTeX file and check every reference against Retraction Watch.

rwcheck batch-bib FILE [--db PATH] [--api URL] [--report-dir DIR]

Arguments

Argument Description FILE Path to a .bib (BibTeX) file.

Options

Option Default Description --report-dir DIR same dir as .bib Directory to write report files

DOI/PMID extraction

For each BibTeX entry the tool looks for identifiers in:

  • doi field
  • url field (extracts DOI from doi.org URLs)
  • pmid field
  • eprint field when eprinttype = {pubmed}

Output

A summary table is printed, then retracted entries are listed, then report paths:

  Total references         42
  Retracted                 2
  Clean (not found)        38
  Unchecked (no DOI/PMID)   2

⚠ Retracted entries:
  ✗ [smith2010] Smith et al. 2010 — Retraction | Cell

Reports written:
  Markdown → refs_rwcheck.md
  HTML     → refs_rwcheck.html
  JSON     → refs_rwcheck.json

Examples

rwcheck batch-bib refs.bib
rwcheck batch-bib refs.bib --report-dir ./output/
rwcheck batch-bib refs.bib --api http://localhost:8000

docs.title: rwcheck update
docs.text:
Download the latest Retraction Watch CSV and rebuild the local database.

rwcheck update [--db PATH] [--url URL] [--force]

Options

Option Default Description --db PATH data/rw.sqlite Target database path --url URL GitLab CSV URL Source URL for the Retraction Watch CSV --force False Rebuild even if the CSV has not changed (SHA-256 check)

The update is skipped if the remote CSV SHA-256 matches the last build. Use --force to rebuild unconditionally.

Examples

# Normal update (skips if unchanged)
rwcheck update

# Force rebuild
rwcheck update --force

# Custom DB path and URL
rwcheck update --db /opt/rw/rw.sqlite --url https://example.com/custom.csv

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python 3.10 or later
  • A writable directory for the SQLite database (default: data/rw.sqlite)

docs.title: Install from PyPI
docs.text:
pip install rwcheck

This installs the rwcheck CLI, the Python library, and all runtime dependencies.

docs.title: Install from source
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/your-org/rwcheck.git
cd rwcheck
pip install -e ".[dev]"

The [dev] extra adds pytest, ruff, and mypy.

docs.title: Build the local database
docs.text:
RWCheck queries a local SQLite file. Build it once after installation:

# Download the latest CSV from GitLab and build the DB
rwcheck update

The database is written to data/rw.sqlite by default. Set RW_DB_PATH to use a different path:

RW_DB_PATH=/opt/rwcheck/rw.sqlite rwcheck update

To rebuild from a local CSV file:

build-rw-db --csv retraction_watch.csv --db data/rw.sqlite

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text: Variable Default Description RW_DB_PATH data/rw.sqlite Path to the SQLite database RW_CSV_URL GitLab URL Source URL for rwcheck update RATE_LIMIT 60/minute REST API rate limit (e.g. 120/minute) UPDATE_INTERVAL_HOURS 24 Auto-update interval for the REST API

docs.title: Docker
docs.text:
Run the REST API in a container with a persistent volume for the database:

docker build -t rwcheck:latest .

docker run -p 8000:8000 \
  -v "$PWD/data:/app/data" \
  rwcheck:latest

On first start the container automatically downloads and builds the database. The browser UI is available at http://localhost:8000 and the OpenAPI docs at http://localhost:8000/docs.

docs.title: Environment overrides
docs.text:
docker run -p 8000:8000 \
  -v "$PWD/data:/app/data" \
  -e RATE_LIMIT=120/minute \
  -e UPDATE_INTERVAL_HOURS=12 \
  rwcheck:latest

docs.title: Docs extras
docs.text:
To build or serve this documentation locally:

pip install "rwcheck[docs]"
mkdocs serve          # live preview at http://127.0.0.1:8000
mkdocs build          # build static site to site/

Or use the Makefile shortcuts:

make docs-serve
make docs

docs.title: Python API
docs.text: RWCheck exposes a simple Python API for programmatic lookups. All three functions query the local SQLite database directly — no HTTP round-trips.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: pip install rwcheck

docs.title: Import
docs.text:
import rwcheck

# or import individual functions
from rwcheck import check_doi, check_pmid, check_batch

docs.title: Database path resolution
docs.text:
All functions accept an optional db_path keyword argument. When omitted the path is resolved in order:

  1. db_path keyword argument
  2. RW_DB_PATH environment variable
  3. "data/rw.sqlite" (relative to the current working directory)
import os

# Set globally for the process
os.environ["RW_DB_PATH"] = "/opt/rwcheck/rw.sqlite"

result = rwcheck.check_doi("10.1038/nature12345")  # uses /opt/rwcheck/rw.sqlite

docs.title: rwcheck.api.check_doi(doi, *, db_path=None)
docs.text:
Check whether doi appears in Retraction Watch.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default doi str

Raw DOI string (URL prefix and doi: prefix are stripped internally).

required db_path str | Path | None

Path to the SQLite database. Defaults to the RW_DB_PATH environment variable or "data/rw.sqlite".

None

Returns:

Type Description dict

{"query": str, "matched": bool, "matches": list[dict], "meta": dict}

docs.title: rwcheck.api.check_pmid(pmid, *, db_path=None)
docs.text:
Check whether pmid appears in Retraction Watch.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default pmid int | str

PubMed ID (integer or numeric string).

required db_path str | Path | None

Path to the SQLite database.

None

Returns:

Type Description dict

{"query": int|str, "matched": bool, "matches": list[dict], "meta": dict}

docs.title: rwcheck.api.check_batch(dois=None, pmids=None, *, db_path=None)
docs.text:
Check a list of DOIs and/or PMIDs against Retraction Watch.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default dois list[str] | None

List of raw DOI strings.

None pmids list[int | str] | None

List of PubMed IDs (integers or strings).

None db_path str | Path | None

Path to the SQLite database.

None

Returns:

Type Description str

JSON string with keys results (list of per-query dicts) and meta. Each result has query, query_type, matched, matches.

docs.title: check_doi / check_pmid
docs.text:
{
    "query":   "10.1038/nature12345",  # original query string
    "matched": False,                  # True if ≥1 record found
    "matches": [],                     # list of RecordSummary dicts (see below)
    "meta": {
        "dataset_version": "abc123def456...",  # first 16 hex chars of CSV SHA-256
        "built_at":        "2024-06-01T12:00:00",
        "row_count":       "45231",
        "source_url":      "https://gitlab.com/...",
        "csv_sha256":      "abc123...",
    }
}

docs.title: check_batch
docs.text:
Returns a JSON string (not a dict) for easy serialisation:

json_str = rwcheck.check_batch(
    dois=["10.1038/nature12345"],
    pmids=[12345678],
)
import json
data = json.loads(json_str)
# data["results"]  → list of per-query dicts
# data["meta"]     → dataset provenance dict

Each item in results:

{
    "query":      "10.1038/nature12345",
    "query_type": "doi",    # "doi" or "pmid"
    "matched":    False,
    "matches":    [],
}

docs.title: Match record fields
docs.text: Field Type Description record_id int Retraction Watch internal record ID title str \| None Title of the retracted paper journal str \| None Journal name publisher str \| None Publisher name author str \| None Author list country str \| None Country of corresponding author retraction_date str \| None Date of retraction (YYYY-MM-DD or partial) retraction_nature str \| None "Retraction", "Correction", "Expression of Concern", … reason str \| None Semicolon-separated retraction reasons original_paper_doi str \| None Normalised DOI of the original paper original_paper_doi_raw str \| None DOI as it appears in the CSV retraction_doi str \| None Normalised DOI of the retraction notice retraction_doi_raw str \| None Retraction notice DOI as in CSV original_paper_pmid int \| None PubMed ID of the original paper retraction_pmid int \| None PubMed ID of the retraction notice paywalled str \| None "Yes" / "No" / "Free" urls str \| None Semicolon-separated related URLs

docs.title: Check a single DOI
docs.text:
import rwcheck

result = rwcheck.check_doi("10.1038/nature12345")

if result["matched"]:
    for match in result["matches"]:
        print(match["retraction_nature"], "|", match["journal"])
        print("Retracted:", match["retraction_date"])
else:
    print("Not found in Retraction Watch")

docs.title: Check a single PMID
docs.text:
result = rwcheck.check_pmid(12345678)

print("Matched:", result["matched"])
print("Dataset built:", result["meta"]["built_at"])

docs.title: Batch check (DOIs + PMIDs)
docs.text:
import json
import rwcheck

json_str = rwcheck.check_batch(
    dois=[
        "10.1038/nature12345",
        "10.1016/j.cell.2009.10.015",
    ],
    pmids=[12345678, 99999999],
)

data = json.loads(json_str)
for item in data["results"]:
    status = "RETRACTED" if item["matched"] else "ok"
    print(f"[{status}] {item['query_type']}:{item['query']}")

docs.title: Use a custom DB path
docs.text:
result = rwcheck.check_doi(
    "10.1038/nature12345",
    db_path="/opt/rwcheck/rw.sqlite",
)

docs.title: Pipeline integration
docs.text:
import csv
import json
import rwcheck

with open("dois.csv") as f:
    reader = csv.DictReader(f)
    dois = [row["doi"] for row in reader]

data = json.loads(rwcheck.check_batch(dois=dois))
retracted = [r for r in data["results"] if r["matched"]]

print(f"{len(retracted)}/{len(dois)} DOIs found in Retraction Watch")
for r in retracted:
    print(" -", r["query"])

docs.title: REST API
docs.text: The rwcheck REST API is a self-hosted FastAPI service that exposes all lookup functionality over HTTP. It includes a browser UI, OpenAPI docs, rate limiting, and a background auto-update scheduler.

docs.title: Starting the server
docs.text:
Local (development)Docker 
pip install rwcheck
rwcheck update           # build the DB first
make api                 # or: uvicorn rw_api.main:app --reload

docker run -p 8000:8000 -v "$PWD/data:/app/data" rwcheck:latest

The browser UI is at http://localhost:8000 and the OpenAPI (Swagger) docs are at http://localhost:8000/docs.

docs.title: GET /health
docs.text:
Liveness check. Returns 200 OK if the service is running.

Response 

{ "status": "ok", "db_exists": true }

docs.title: GET /meta
docs.text:
Dataset provenance — when the DB was last built and from where.

Response 

{
  "dataset_version": "abc123def4567890",
  "built_at": "2024-06-01T12:00:00",
  "row_count": "45231",
  "source_url": "https://gitlab.com/crossref/retraction-watch-data/...",
  "csv_sha256": "abc123..."
}

docs.title: GET /stats
docs.text:
Aggregate statistics about the dataset.

Response 

{
  "total_records": 45231,
  "total_journals": 8412,
  "total_countries": 94,
  "doi_coverage": 39801,
  "pmid_coverage": 32100,
  "by_year": [["2000", 12], ["2001", 34], ...],
  "top_journals": [["PLOS ONE", 2100], ...],
  "by_country": [["United States", 12000], ...],
  "meta": { ... }
}

docs.title: GET /check/doi/{doi}
docs.text:
Check a single DOI.

Path parameter

Parameter Description doi URL-encoded DOI (e.g. 10.1038%2Fnature12345)

Example 

curl "http://localhost:8000/check/doi/10.1038%2Fnature12345"

Response 

{
  "query": "10.1038/nature12345",
  "matched": false,
  "matches": [],
  "meta": { "dataset_version": "...", "built_at": "...", "row_count": "45231", ... }
}

When matched: 

{
  "query": "10.1016/j.cell.2009.10.015",
  "matched": true,
  "matches": [
    {
      "record_id": 12345,
      "title": "Example Paper",
      "journal": "Cell",
      "retraction_date": "2010-01-15",
      "retraction_nature": "Retraction",
      "reason": "Data Fabrication",
      "original_paper_doi": "10.1016/j.cell.2009.10.015",
      "retraction_doi": "10.1016/j.cell.2010.01.010",
      ...
    }
  ],
  "meta": { ... }
}

docs.title: GET /check/pmid/{pmid}
docs.text:
Check a single PubMed ID.

Path parameter

Parameter Description pmid Integer PubMed ID

Example 

curl "http://localhost:8000/check/pmid/12345678"

Response — same shape as /check/doi/{doi}, with "query": 12345678.

docs.title: POST /check/batch
docs.text:
Check a list of DOIs and/or PMIDs in a single request.

Request body 

{
  "dois":  ["10.1038/nature12345", "10.1016/j.cell.2009.10.015"],
  "pmids": [12345678, 99999999]
}

Example 

curl -X POST "http://localhost:8000/check/batch" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"dois": ["10.1038/nature12345"], "pmids": [12345678]}'

Response 

{
  "results": [
    {
      "query": "10.1038/nature12345",
      "query_type": "doi",
      "matched": false,
      "matches": []
    },
    {
      "query": 12345678,
      "query_type": "pmid",
      "matched": false,
      "matches": []
    }
  ],
  "meta": { ... }
}

Rate limit — defaults to 60 requests/minute per IP. Override with the RATE_LIMIT environment variable.

docs.title: POST /check/bib
docs.text:
Upload a BibTeX file and check every reference.

Request - Content-Type: multipart/form-data - Field: file — a .bib file

Example 

curl -X POST "http://localhost:8000/check/bib" \
  -F "file=@refs.bib"

Response 

{
  "total": 42,
  "retracted": 2,
  "clean": 38,
  "unchecked": 2,
  "results": [
    {
      "key": "smith2010",
      "title": "Example Paper",
      "doi": "10.1016/j.cell.2009.10.015",
      "pmid": null,
      "matched": true,
      "matches": [ { ... } ]
    },
    ...
  ],
  "meta": { ... }
}

docs.title: RecordSummary
docs.text:
Fields returned inside every matches array:

Field Type Description record_id integer Retraction Watch record ID title string \| null Title of the retracted paper journal string \| null Journal name publisher string \| null Publisher author string \| null Author list country string \| null Corresponding author country retraction_date string \| null Retraction date (ISO 8601 or partial) retraction_nature string \| null Retraction / Correction / Expression of Concern reason string \| null Semicolon-separated retraction reasons original_paper_doi string \| null Normalised original-paper DOI original_paper_doi_raw string \| null Original-paper DOI as in dataset retraction_doi string \| null Normalised retraction-notice DOI retraction_doi_raw string \| null Retraction-notice DOI as in dataset original_paper_pmid integer \| null Original paper PMID retraction_pmid integer \| null Retraction notice PMID paywalled string \| null "Yes" / "No" / "Free" urls string \| null Semicolon-separated related URLs

docs.title: Client examples
docs.text:
curlPython (httpx)Python (requests) 
# Single DOI
curl "http://localhost:8000/check/doi/10.1038%2Fnature12345" | jq .

# Batch
curl -X POST "http://localhost:8000/check/batch" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"dois": ["10.1038/nature12345"], "pmids": [12345678]}' | jq .

import httpx

BASE = "http://localhost:8000"

# Single DOI
r = httpx.get(f"{BASE}/check/doi/10.1038%2Fnature12345")
print(r.json()["matched"])

# Batch
r = httpx.post(f"{BASE}/check/batch", json={
    "dois": ["10.1038/nature12345"],
    "pmids": [12345678],
})
for item in r.json()["results"]:
    print(item["query"], "→", "RETRACTED" if item["matched"] else "ok")

import requests

BASE = "http://localhost:8000"

# Single DOI
r = requests.get(f"{BASE}/check/doi/10.1038%2Fnature12345")
print(r.json()["matched"])

# Batch
r = requests.post(f"{BASE}/check/batch", json={
    "dois": ["10.1038/nature12345"],
    "pmids": [12345678],
})
for item in r.json()["results"]:
    status = "RETRACTED" if item["matched"] else "ok"
    print(f"[{status}] {item['query']}")

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Environment variable Default Description RW_DB_PATH /app/data/rw.sqlite Path to the SQLite database RW_CSV_URL GitLab URL Source URL for auto-updates RATE_LIMIT 60/minute Rate limit per IP (e.g. 120/minute) UPDATE_INTERVAL_HOURS 24 Background auto-update interval

The API auto-updates the database on a background schedule. The first update runs at startup if the database does not yet exist.
